subject: Clarify processor/service-provider boundaries and subprocessor obligations for CPRA addendum
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@northbridge.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CPRA addendum: confirmation of SP vs processor and subprocessor obligations

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier. We are running Northbridge's legal intake and need to confirm a couple of items before our procurement team will proceed:

1) In the CPRA addendum you sent, Redwood is listed as a "service provider" for the specific use-cases described. We want to confirm that telemetry/usage logs that include customer account identifiers will be treated strictly under the service-provider (limited-use) carve-out and will not be sold or used for other purposes.

2) We have a specific requirement to get a list of subprocessors that could handle unredacted telemetry (syslogs, debug dumps) and the timing for notice before onboarding. Can you provide your current subprocessor roster and your typical notice window? For any onshore fallback providers we also need confirmation of encryption-in-transit and at-rest controls.

3) Last: because Northbridge processes sensitive healthcare-adjacent metadata, our counsel prefers explicit language about cross-state transfers — specifically that you will not transfer data outside the U.S. without written consent, and that any cross-state transfers for support will be limited and logged with audit evidence.

We attached our standard CPRA addendum template for your redline. Procurement is targeting execution in the next three weeks if we can resolve these items.

Thanks,
Maria
Contracts Manager | Northbridge Systems

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum: confirmation of SP vs processor and subprocessor obligations

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and for the template. I looped in Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Privacy/Policy) to help.

High-level answers up front:
- Redwood confirms we will act as a "service provider" (limited-use) for the specified processing under the CPRA addendum, and we will not use customer data outside the scope of the agreement for advertising or resale. We will update the addendum redline to reflect explicit limited-use language and the prohibition on sale.
- Subprocessor roster & notice: we maintain a current roster and follow a 14-calendar-day advance notice for non-emergency onboardings. For emergency (incident-driven) onboarding we provide notice as soon as practicable and document all activity. We will include the roster and notice language in the redline.
- Cross-state transfers: we can commit to a U.S.-only transfer restriction absent prior written consent, with an exception path for documented support escalations that are logged and audited. We'll propose an onshore-fallback flow in the addendum with explicit logging/audit-paper trail requirements.

I'll attach a focused redline to your template with the proposed language for the three bullets above. Can you confirm whether your counsel needs SOC 2 type II reports and whether the RMF evidence (KMS/HSM config) should be provided as part of the vendor pack?

Next steps: Marissa will circulate the redline by EOD 5/12 and we can set a short call to walk the changes.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@northbridge.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: CPRA addendum redline and subprocessor roster (attached)

Hi Maria — attaching our redline and current subprocessor roster. Highlights:
- Added explicit limited-use / non-sale clause under Section 2(b).
- Inserted 14-day notice for planned subprocessor additions and a documented emergency-onboard exception with post-facto notice and attestations.
- Added an "Onshore fallback and documented support flow" clause: temporary cross-state access for support is allowed only when logged, limited in scope, and subject to prior approval from an authorized security contact (we propose a contact exchange).
- Attached: CPRA_Addendum_Redline_20270512.docx, Redwood_DPA_Tracker.xlsx (subprocessor roster).

Aditya from our infra team is cc'd — he can confirm the encryption controls and KMS handling for the onshore fallback.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@northbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum redline and subprocessor roster (encryption + controls)

Hi Maria — quick note from Infra:

- All customer telemetry in transit uses TLS 1.2+; storage uses AES-256 at rest with envelope encryption. Keys are in a customer/tenant-segmented KMS; we can provide a whitepaper and a redacted KMS configuration snapshot for your security review.
- For onshore-fallback providers we require access via a bastion + short-lived credentials and we log session-level events to a tamper-evident audit store (retention and export available).
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and scoped control narratives; if you need full reports we will route the request through our security share process (we'll need an NDA/POA as standard).

If Northbridge wants proof-of-control artifacts in the vendor pack, Laura from Trust & Safety can coordinate delivery.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@northbridge.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum redline and subprocessor roster (attached)

Priya/Marissa/Aditya — this is helpful, thanks. Our counsel reviewed the redline and had two quick asks: 

1) Replace the 14-day notice with a contractual "notice and objection" workflow that allows Northbridge to object to a planned subprocessor within 10 business days; if not objected to, the onboarding proceeds.
2) Add an explicit requirement that any emergency onshore-fallback onboarding be followed by an incident packet that includes (a) justification, (b) list of individuals who accessed data, and (c) exported audit logs within 7 business days.

Procurement is comfortable keeping the contract cadence tight — if you can accept the objection workflow and the incident packet timing, we're ready to move to internal approvals and target signature by 5/28.

One more note: Samir asked whether DocuSign execution is acceptable; yes — we can do e-signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Maria
Contracts Manager | Northbridge Systems
